targets.authors: Basol, M., Roozenbeek, J., & van der Linden, S.
targets.title: Good news about Bad News: Gamified inoculation boosts confidence and cognitive immunity against fake news.
targets.evidence_quote: Here we report four parallel attempts to replicate (and extend) the Basol et al. (2020) study.
targets.outcome_quote: The less good news is that the Bad News Game also reduced ratings of the truth of true Tweets. That effect, too, was substantial and significant in each replication study. There were hints that the BNG had a slightly bigger impact on the perceived truth of false than true Tweets in two of the studies. But that 3-way interaction was statistically significant in only one of the studies, and mean-level and ROC analyses across all four experiments provided no support for the hypothesis that playing the BNG improved discrimination between true and false Tweets across these studies.
targets.outcome_reasoning: All four teams recover the false-tweet rating effect, but the central message is that comparable decreases for true tweets undermine its interpretation as improved misinformation discrimination. Team names are used rather than numbered studies; one original paper is targeted.
